CardDefinition.description: One card as the engine sees it: its faces and what they do. Nothing about price, art or set; those live in the Scryfall object the card came from.

Face.description: One face of a card: the printed characteristics, CR 109.3, and its abilities. Power and toughness stay as printed so "*" survives; the engine reads the number when there is one.

TypeLine.description: The type line, CR 205: supertypes, types, subtypes.

PrintedStat.description: Printed power or toughness: a number, or a characteristic-defining marker such as "*".

Ability.description: The six shapes an ability can take, CR 113.3, plus the keyword form. Every line of a card's text is one of these.

Cost.description: What a player pays, CR 118. Mana is written as printed ("{1}{G}", "{X}{X}"); everything else is a record. A cost that asks for a choice takes it with the activation, so the engine never suspends a payment.

Condition.description: A yes-or-no question about the game: an intervening "if" on a trigger, the "as long as" of a static ability, the "if" of an effect. Ability words are conditions here, not nodes of their own.

ClassLevel.description: A Class card's level, CR 716: the cost to reach it and what it adds.

AlternativeCost.description: A printed alternative cost, CR 118.9: "you may pay {B} rather than pay this spell's mana cost", with the condition the printed line gates it on — "if a creature died this turn". The spell is cast for Cost instead of its mana cost, and only while OnlyIf holds as the cost is chosen (CR 601.2b, where one alternative cost is chosen and CR 601.2f, where it is paid). Leave OnlyIf null for an ungated one. It belongs on the Face rather than on an ability because it is not a thing the card does: it is an option offered as the spell is cast, before any ability of it exists. A face may print more than one, and the caster picks at most one of them (CR 601.2b) — the list is the printed alternatives, never a way of saying "and". It is not AdditionalCosts, which is CR 118.8 and is paid on top of the mana cost; a reading that puts an alternative cost there makes the spell cost both, which is a different card. It is not MayPay either: that is a choice made as the spell resolves, and this one is made as the spell is cast, before targets are legal. And it is not the play-permission flags on MayPlayFromZone, which grant a cast from another zone; this is the printed line on the card itself, whatever zone it is cast from.

ActivatedAbility.description: "[Cost]: [Effect]", CR 602. Loyalty abilities carry a LoyaltyCost; mana abilities are recognised by the engine, CR 605. PayOnlyWith is the printed rider "activate only using mana produced by a creature" read as a colour restriction: the mana spent on this ability's cost must be of those colours (CR 106.6b, the spend restriction's other half). Leave it null for the ordinary case, where any mana pays. PayOnlyFrom is the other half of that rider: "activate only using mana produced by artifacts" names the source the mana came from rather than its colour, and a colour cannot say it (CR 106.6b). The filter describes the permanent whose mana ability produced the mana. Set one field or the other, never both — a card prints one restriction, and two would be read as an "and" no card asked for. A restriction neither can express goes to a primitive request rather than being dropped, because paying with the wrong mana is a different game action, not a rounding error. PayOnlyWithChosenColorKey is the third reading of the same rider, for "activate only using mana of the chosen color" (CR 106.6b restricts what mana may be spent; CR 601.2h is where the payment is made and the restriction bites). It names the key of the earlier ChooseValue(Color) step, so the restriction is whatever colour this object chose rather than a printed one. It belongs to the same one-of-three group as PayOnlyWith and PayOnlyFrom: set at most one, because two riders would be read as an "and" no card prints.

KeywordAbility.description: A keyword from CR 702 with its parameters: "Ward {2}" is Cost, "Bushido 2" is N, "Protection from red" and "Affinity for artifacts" are Of, "Partner with Name" is Detail. Cost is a printed mana string and takes nothing else. A keyword whose cost has a non-mana part — escape's "{1}{B}{B}, Exile four other cards from your graveyard" (CR 702.138a), and the "sacrifice a creature" half of several others — puts the whole cost in Costs as Cost records instead, mana included as a ManaCost entry, and leaves Cost null. Set one or the other, never both: two spellings of the same cost is how a card silently gets paid twice or not at all. Set Repeatable when the printed word says the cost may be paid more than once as the spell is cast: multikicker (CR 702.32b) and replicate-shaped keywords. Plain kicker (CR 702.32a) is paid once or not at all and leaves it false. A repeatable keyword is what makes the TimesKicked amount countable; without the flag, casting refuses a second payment, so a multikicker card translated without it is castable but never kicked twice. OfPlayer: "enchant player", "enchant opponent" (CR 702.5b): what this Aura may enchant when it is a player rather than an object. An enchant ability with neither Of nor OfPlayer admits any object or player; one with Of only admits objects. RememberAs is for the keywords that set an object aside for a later ability to name. Hideaway exiles one of the cards it looked at (CR 702.75a) and a second ability on the same permanent then says "you may play the exiled card"; the keyword stores what it exiled under this key and that ability names it with a Remembered selector. Without it the second ability has nothing to point at, because the keyword's own text is not written out on the card. Set it only for a keyword that puts an object somewhere — a key on a keyword that sets nothing aside is noise nothing reads.

SpellAbility.description: What an instant or sorcery does when it resolves, CR 113.3a.

StaticAbility.description: A continuous effect from a static ability, CR 604. Applies to objects via To or to players via Players.

TriggeredAbility.description: "When", "whenever", "at", CR 603. Where is the zone the ability functions in.

ChooseCost.description: "Pay {2} or sacrifice a creature": one of several costs, chosen when paying.

DiscardCost.description: "Discard a card" as a cost, CR 701.8a. RememberAs is the same idea as SacrificeCost's: the discarded cards are stored under the key so "if you do, [it]" can name them, and it stays null when nothing refers back.

DiscardSelfCost.description: "Discard this card": the card the ability is on is the one discarded, and no other card can pay it. This is the cost cycling asks for — "[Cost], Discard this card: Draw a card" (CR 702.29a) — and the same shape jump-start and other discard-this-card abilities use. Use DiscardCost only when the text says "discard a card", where the player chooses which; a player must not be able to pay a discard-this-card cost with a different card.

ExileFromZoneCost.description: "Exile a creature card from your graveyard", "exile N cards from your hand". RememberAs stores the exiled cards under a key (CR 701.10a) so an effect can say "if you do, [it]" — "exile a creature card from your graveyard: put a +1/+1 counter on this for each of its colours". Null when nothing refers back.

LoyaltyCost.description: A loyalty ability's cost: +N, −N or 0, CR 606.

PayManaCost.description: Generic mana whose amount is counted from the game rather than printed, CR 118.8: "unless that player pays {X}, where X is this creature's power". Generic is the number of generic mana to pay, evaluated when the cost is announced (CR 601.2h); Colored is any printed coloured part paid alongside it ("{R} plus {X}"), written as printed. Use ManaCost for everything a card prints as a fixed symbol string, including "{X}" spelled with the spell's own X — this record is only for an amount the game has to count.

SacrificeCost.description: "Sacrifice a creature": the player chooses which permanent they control is sacrificed (CR 701.17a). Set RememberAs when the effect refers back to what paid — "sacrifice a creature: add mana equal to its power", "if you do, draw cards equal to its toughness". The cost payment stores the objects it sacrificed under the key as they last existed on the battlefield (CR 608.2g reads a sacrificed permanent's last known information), and the effect names them with a Remembered selector. Leave it null when nothing looks back: a key nothing reads is noise in the file.

TapOther.description: "Tap an untapped creature you control": tap other permanents matching a filter.

TapUntappedCost.description: Convoke, improvise and "waterbend": tap untapped permanents in place of generic mana.

Adamant.description: Three or more mana of one color was spent to cast this spell.

AttackedThisTurn.description: "if you attacked with two or more creatures this turn": how many creatures a player declared as attackers this turn, compared against Min, CR 506.2 and 508.1. Counted over the whole turn and every combat phase in it, not just the current one, and a creature that was declared an attacker still counts after it has left combat or died. Raid is the same question with a minimum of one and is kept because the ability word is printed; use this record whenever the card names a number, and prefer it over Raid when the number is anything but one.

ChoiceIs.description: An earlier choice had a given value: "if the chosen color is red".

Compare.description: Any two amounts compared: "if your life total is less than an opponent's".

Controls.description: "if you control three or more artifacts": a count of objects compared to a number.

Corrupted.description: An opponent has three or more poison counters.

Coven.description: Three or more creatures with different powers.

CreatedTokenThisTurn.description: "if you created a token this turn": a player put one or more tokens onto the battlefield this turn, CR 111.1 ("Some effects put tokens onto the battlefield"). Counted over the whole turn and every effect in it, and a token that has since left the battlefield or ceased to exist still counts — the same reading AttackedThisTurn takes of a creature that has died. What narrows it to a kind of token when the card does ("created a Treasure token this turn"), read against the token as it was created rather than as it is now.

Descend.description: Descend N: N or more permanent cards in your graveyard.

Ferocious.description: You control a creature with power 4 or greater.

FirstTimeThisTurn.description: "the first time this ability resolves each turn".

Formidable.description: Creatures you control have total power 8 or greater.

GiftPromised.description: "if the gift was promised", CR 702.174b: the caster of a spell with gift chose, as they cast it, to promise the gift to an opponent, and the spell's "if the gift was promised" clauses now apply. Promising is a choice made on casting, so this is answered from the spell's record of that choice, not from anything on the battlefield. Who names the player the gift was promised to when the card asks about them; leave it null for the plain "if the gift was promised" reading.

Matches.description: The selected object matches a filter: "if it's a creature card".

Paradox.description: You cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand this turn.

Raid.description: You attacked with a creature this turn.

Revolt.description: A permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn.

SpellMastery.description: Two or more instant and/or sorcery cards in your graveyard.

StoredIs.description: A stored count compared: "if two or more cards were discarded this way".

TargetsAre.description: The chosen targets satisfy a filter, checked at resolution.

Effect.description: One instruction of a resolving spell or ability. The structural records combine instructions; the verbs in Effects.Verbs.cs and the keyword actions in Effects.Actions.cs do things. This is the whole list, and it is the name table.

Amount.description: A number a card refers to. Most are fixed; the rest are counted from the game when the effect resolves. Every derived record is registered here, and a test asserts that the list is complete.

ObjectFilter.description: A description of objects. Every field is optional and every set field must hold. This is the noun phrase of the game: "another nontoken creature you control with power 4 or greater" is one filter. Anything the fields cannot say goes in Also. The fields are joined with "and", except the two subtype lists, which are "any of": Subtypes ["Forest", "Island"] is "a Forest or Island card" (CR 205.3, an object has each of its subtypes), and NotSubtypes excludes an object that has any listed one; "a Forest Island" (both) is two nested filters, not one list. The fixed fields otherwise cannot say "or": "attacking or blocking creature" is not Attacking plus Blocking, which would match nothing. That one disjunction is common enough to have its own field — InCombat, true for a creature that is an attacking or a blocking creature (CR 506.2, 506.4) and false for one that is neither. Any other disjunction is written with AnyOf in Also. "Attacking or blocking creature" is InCombat and has no second spelling: there is no AttackingOrBlocking field, and writing Attacking beside Blocking matches nothing. HasBasicLandType is "a land card with a basic land type", CR 205.3i: true when the object has any of Forest, Island, Mountain, Plains or Swamp among its subtypes, whatever else it also has, and false for a nonbasic land with none of them. It is not Supertype.Basic — a shockland and a dual land have a basic land type and are not basic — and it is not a Subtypes list, which is joined with "and" and so cannot say "any of the five". ManaCostIs is the printed mana cost read as a whole string, CR 202.1: the list is "any of", and an object matches when its printed cost is one of the listed symbol strings exactly as printed — ["{0}", "{1}"] is "with mana value 0 or 1" said the way a card that cares about the printed cost says it. It is not ManaValue, which counts the cost and so admits "{W}" for 1 and cannot tell "{0}" from a land's absent cost; use ManaValue whenever the card prints a number, and this only where the printed symbols themselves are named. An object with no printed mana cost matches no entry, and an empty list matches nothing at all rather than everything. NotInCommanderIdentityColors is "colors not in your commander's color identity", CR 903.4: true admits an object of a colour outside that identity and false admits one wholly inside it. It is CastFrom and NotCastFrom are the zone a spell was cast from, CR 601.3 read as a description of the spell rather than of the caster: "players cannot cast spells from anywhere other than their hands" is a CantCastSpells whose Matching filter has Spell true and NotCastFrom Hand. Set one or the other, never both — a card names the zone it allows or the one it forbids, and both together admits nothing (L038) — and only on a filter that describes a spell: a permanent was never cast from anywhere the game still remembers. It is not the CastFromZone condition, which asks where this card was cast from and can say nothing about anyone else spell. the narrow spelling of the one colour-set reference the pilot asked for and takes no colours of its own, because the set is the game's and not the card's. Never write it as a Colors or NotColors list, which would fix at translation time a set that depends on the deck.

PlayerFilter.description: Who qualifies for a player choice or target.

ReplacedEvent.description: The event a replacement effect watches for, CR 614. The ability's With effect runs instead of the event, with Triggering bound to the object the event was about.

ContinuousEffect.description: What a continuous effect does to the objects or players it applies to, CR 611–613. Each record belongs to one layer, which the interpreter reads from the record type.

Selector.description: Which objects an instruction acts on. A selector names the objects; an ObjectFilter describes them. Targets are selectors, and so are "each creature", "this permanent" and "the exiled card".

PlayerRef.description: Which player or players an instruction means. "You" is the controller of the ability; everything else is relative to that or to the objects in play.

Trigger.description: The event a triggered ability watches for, CR 603. Each record names the event and describes the objects or players it must involve. The interpreter binds Triggering selectors to the matched objects.

Comparison.description: A comparison of some quantity against an amount: "power 4 or greater" is Ge 4.

AddMana.description: "Add {G}{G}", "add one mana of any color", "add X mana of the chosen color". Set SpendOnlyOn for a restricted mana: "add {C}. Spend this mana only to cast artifact spells" (CR 106.6a) — the filter describes what the mana may be spent on, and mana with a restriction is otherwise ordinary mana that empties from the pool as usual (CR 106.6b). Say "only to cast creature spells" as ObjectFilter(Spell: true, Types: CardType.Creature) and "only to activate abilities" with an ability filter; a restriction the filter cannot express goes to a primitive request rather than being dropped, because unrestricted mana is a different card. Set Key when a later step has to say "that mana": CR 106.6 lets a mana instruction create a delayed triggered ability that fires when the mana it produced is spent, and the ManaSpent trigger names the mana by this key. Mana is not an object, so a Remembered selector cannot hold it and there is nothing else to point at. Leave it null otherwise — a key nothing reads is noise in the file.

Apply.description: "target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn", "gains flying until end of turn", "becomes a copy".

ApplyToPlayer.description: "You have no maximum hand size until end of turn": a continuous effect on a player.

Behold.description: "Behold a Dragon": reveal one from hand or choose one you control, remembered under a key.

ChangeTarget.description: "Change the target of target spell with a single target", CR 115.7: the spell or ability keeps resolving but points somewhere else. What selects the spell or ability on the stack; To names the new target when the card names it ("change its target to this creature") and is left null when the card lets a player choose. Set AllTargets for "you may choose new targets for it" (CR 114.6), which is the weaker action: it may leave the targets as they are, while a change must alter at least one (CR 115.7b). Legality is rechecked on resolution, so an illegal change is simply not made.

ChooseMode.description: "Choose one —", "choose two", "choose one or more". Entwine and escalate set Max to the mode count. MaxIf is a mode count that depends on the game as the spell is cast: "choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may choose both instead" is Max 1 with MaxIf a Controls condition over a filter of isCommander and MaxIfMet 2. The modes are announced as the spell is cast (CR 601.2b, which sends the count to CR 700.2), so the condition is read at that announcement and never again: a commander that leaves later changes nothing. MaxIfMet is the ceiling while the condition holds and must exceed Max, or the rider says nothing (L024); Min is the same either way. Never an If around a ChooseMode, which would read the condition on resolution, and never two ChooseModes for one printed list. Budget is a mode count spent rather than counted: "choose modes with total cost {5} or less" over modes that each print a price. The modes are still announced as the spell is cast (CR 601.2b sends the choice to CR 700.2), and the announcement is legal only while the prices of the modes chosen total no more than the budget. Every mode then needs its own Cost and a priced mode needs a budget to spend against, so the two fields are set together or not at all (L032). Max stops meaning the number of modes when a budget rules them — leave it at its default and let the prices do the counting — and SameModeTwice is what "you may choose the same mode more than once" says here, each repeat paying its price again.

ChooseNumberSecretly.description: "Each player secretly chooses a number, then those numbers are revealed", CR 700.2 with 101.4: one step in which every player Who admits chooses a number without seeing what the others chose, and the choices are revealed as the step finishes. The reveal is part of this step and never a second one — there is nothing for a later step to reveal, and a choice that was never secret is a different card. The numbers are stored under Key, and the ability reads them back with HighestChosen, LowestChosen and the PlayerWhoChose player reference. Min and Max are the printed bounds where a card prints them; leave them out for an unbounded choice. It is not ChooseValue with ChooseWhat.Number, which is one player choosing in the open and read back as a ChosenNumber, and it is not a ForEachPlayer around one: choices made in APNAP order are made in turn and each player would see the ones before theirs (CR 101.4), which is the whole of what this record says. A secret choice nothing reads back is a lost sentence (L035).

ChooseValue.description: "Choose a color", "choose a creature type", "choose a number": the choice is stored under a key.

CreateEmblem.description: A player gets an emblem (CR 114): an object in the command zone with no characteristics but the abilities the card gave it. Use this only when the card's own text prints those abilities, which is nearly always a planeswalker's ultimate ("You get an emblem with …"). An emblem the rules define rather than the card — the Ring, CR 701.54b — is RingTemptsYou, and the engine supplies its abilities; see that record's remarks.

DealDamage.description: "Deals 3 damage": to objects through To, to players through ToPlayer, or to both when the card names both ("deals 2 damage to target creature and 2 damage to that creature's controller"). The three words "any target" are not both halves written out: they are the AnyTarget selector in To, with ToPlayer left out (CR 115.4). Use the two halves together only when the card really names two things to damage. ExcessTo is "excess damage is dealt to that creature's controller instead": the damage over what was lethal to the creature or planeswalker damaged goes to a player (CR 120.3d defines excess damage as the amount beyond what is needed to destroy it, and CR 702.19c is the trample rule that reads it). Only the excess moves; the rest is dealt as usual, and a creature that takes less than lethal leaves no excess at all. Normally a ControllerOf over the same selector To names. It rides on the damage the card deals, so it needs a To to have an excess to read (L031): damage to a player is never excess. It is not a second DealDamage — a reading that deals the excess as its own instruction has no way to know what was lethal — and it is not trample, which is a KeywordAbility about assigning combat damage before it is dealt. ExcessIf is the gate the printed line puts on that redirection — "if the creature you control has trample, excess damage is dealt to that creature's controller instead", the sentence CR 702.19c is written under — read as the damage is dealt and only about where the excess goes; the damage itself happens either way. Never an If around two copies of the same damage instruction, which is one printed sentence written twice and the reading the translators disagreed over. Leave it null when the card redirects the excess unconditionally, and never set it without ExcessTo (L031), which would gate nothing.

DealDividedDamage.description: "deals 4 damage divided as you choose among one, two, three, or four targets".

DelayedTrigger.description: "At the beginning of the next end step, return it." A trigger created by this effect, CR 603.7. Until is the printed deadline, CR 603.7c: "until end of turn, whenever a creature you control deals damage to a player, draw that many cards" is one DelayedTrigger with Once false and Until UntilEndOfTurn — the ability waits for its event for that long and is gone when the duration ends, whether or not it ever fired. It is the same "this turn" that ends a continuous effect, so it is a Duration and not a condition or a turn count. Leave it null for the ordinary one-shot, whose own event is its end ("at the beginning of the next end step"): a deadline there would either repeat what the event already says or contradict it. Set Once false whenever the printed line says "whenever" inside a duration, and keep it true for the single firing; the two fields answer different questions — how many times, and for how long — and a card that prints a duration and "whenever" prints both.

DistributeCounters.description: "Distribute three +1/+1 counters among one, two, or three target creatures", CR 601.2d: the division is announced as the spell is cast, every named target gets at least one counter, and no more than MaxTargets targets may be chosen. N is the total distributed, Counter the kind, and Among the target selector, whose own Count is the number of targets and is normally left null so MaxTargets rules it. This is the counter twin of DealDividedDamage; do not spell a division as ForEach over targets, which would give every target the whole amount.

EntersAs.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters as a copy, transformed, face down, or under another's control.

EntersTapped.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters tapped.

EntersWithCounters.description: Inside a replacement: the entering object enters with counters.

Flip.description: "Flip it", CR 710.2: a flip permanent is turned upside down and its alternative (FaceRole.Flipped) face's name, types, abilities and power/toughness apply. This is not transform (CR 701.27a), which turns a double-faced card over to its back face, and not FlipCoin, which is CR 705. A flip is one way only — CR 710.4 has no action that unflips — so a card that "returns it to its unflipped state" is a different mechanic and goes to a primitive request. Use this record whenever the printed text says the permanent flips, whatever the layout says.

ForEach.description: "For each creature you control, ...". Inside, Triggering is the current object.

ForEachPlayer.description: "Each player ...", in APNAP order. Inside, TriggeringPlayer is the current player.

If.description: "If you do, ...", "if it's a creature card, ...".

LookAt.description: "Look at target player's hand", "look at the top four cards of your library".

LoseLife.description: "Each opponent loses 3 life." StoreAs is how "the life lost this way" is said, CR 119.4: the life actually lost is stored under that key — the total across every player this one instruction took life from — and a later step reads it as a Stored amount, so "you gain life equal to the life lost this way" is a GainLife whose N is Stored(that key). It is the life the game took, not the number the card asked for: a player at 2 who is asked for 3 loses 2, and CR 119.4 says the effect refers to what was lost. So the key is never a second copy of the amount — writing GainLife with the same Amount the LoseLife carried is a different card, and a Devotion or an X counted twice can differ between the two readings anyway. Leave the key out when nothing on the card refers back.

May.description: "You may ...": the player decides on resolution. Who defaults to you.

MayCast.description: "You may cast it without paying its mana cost", "you may cast that card this turn".

MayPay.description: "You may pay {4}. If you do, ...": a cost offered to a player while the effect resolves, CR 118.12 — "[A player] may [do something]. If [that player] [does, doesn't, or can't], [effect]. The action [do something] is a cost, paid when the spell or ability resolves." Paid is that cost, Then the "if you do" half, Else the "if you don't" half when the card prints one, and Who the player offered the choice, defaulting to you. This is the one spelling of the whole sentence. Do not write it as May wrapping PayCost with a StoreChoiceAs key followed by If(ChoiceIs(key, "yes"), ...): that reads the same to a person and is four records the translator has to agree on instead of one. PayCost stays for a cost the card makes a player pay outright, with no choice and no "if you do". It is the mirror of Unless, not a synonym of it. CR 118.12a: "[do something] unless [a player does something else]" means "[a player] may [do something else]. If [that player] doesn't, [do something]". Unless carries the effect that happens when the cost goes unpaid, which is how "counter it unless its controller pays {3}" is written; MayPay carries the effect that happens when it is paid instead. Which half the card prints is the half the translator keeps, so a card is never rewritten from one into the other.

MayPlay.description: "You may play that card this turn" (lands included). With WithoutPayingManaCost, "you may play the exiled card without paying its mana cost" — hideaway's play, CR 702.75a. A card played this way is played as its type says (CR 305.1 for a land, CR 601 for a spell): a spell is cast without paying its mana cost (CR 118.9), and a land played this way is still the turn's land play and needs a land play left (CR 305.2), because the permission is to play, not an extra play. This is the one spelling of a play permission that waives the cost: MayCast carries the same waiver and cannot play a land, so hideaway's play is never MayCast.

ModifyAmount.description: Inside a replacement: the event happens with its number changed: "draw twice that many", "gain that much life plus 1".

Move.description: The one zone-change verb: "return target creature to its owner's hand", "put it onto the battlefield tapped", "put that card on the bottom of your library". Exile and sacrifice have their own records because the rules name them.

PayCost.description: "Sacrifice a creature", "pay 3 life" — a cost paid inside a resolving effect with no choice offered, CR 118.12. The cost is paid where it stands rather than as part of casting or activating. Any Cost record works here, including PayManaCost for an amount counted from the game. Then is the "if you do" of a mandatory cost: "sacrifice a creature. If you do, draw two cards." The instruction is not a choice — the player pays if they can — but it can fail, because a resolving effect does as much as it can and nothing more (CR 608.2c), and the printed second half runs only when the whole cost was actually paid. A partly paid cost is not paid: an empty board pays no sacrifice, so Then does not run. Leave it null for the bare instruction with nothing hanging on it. Use MayPay for "you may pay {4}. If you do, ..." and Unless for "unless that player pays": both are one record each and neither is spelled as a May or an If wrapped around this one. A PayCost inside a May with a StoreChoiceAs key is the shape MayPay replaced, and a canonical pass collapses it. The two spellings never both apply: a May around a PayCost that carries Then is MayPay's whole sentence written out, and lints as one (L034). Which record a card gets is which half it prints — "you may pay" is MayPay, a bare imperative with an "if you do" is this one.

Prepare.description: Prepare, CR 702.180: the object gains the Prepared designation, which lasts until something takes it away and is not a counter and not an ability. Ask about it with the IsPrepared predicate.

PreventThatDamage.description: Inside a damage replacement: prevent that damage, all of it or an amount.

PutPlayerCounters.description: Poison, energy, experience, rad and ticket counters on a player; negative amounts remove.

Remember.description: Remember the objects a selector resolves to under a key, for later steps.

Reorder.description: "Put them back in any order", "in a random order".

ReplaceWith.description: Inside a replacement: the whole event is replaced by this effect; "instead".

RevealUntil.description: Cascade-shaped: reveal from the top until a match; remember the match and the rest separately.

RingTemptsYou.description: The Ring tempts you (CR 701.54): you get the emblem named The Ring if you do not have it, and then choose a creature you control as your Ring-bearer.

Sacrifice.description: "Sacrifice a creature": the player chooses; "sacrifice it": a selector.

Search.description: "Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." One zone goes in From. A card that searches several at once — "search your graveyard, hand, and library for a card named ..." — puts every zone in Zones in printed order and leaves From alone; the whole search is one action over the union, so a single card is found across all of them (CR 701.23a). Shuffling follows CR 701.23c: a library that was searched is shuffled afterwards and other zones are not, so a multi-zone search with ShuffleAfter set shuffles only the libraries among Zones. Set ShuffleOnlyIfFound for the printed rider "if you do, shuffle" / "shuffle only if you searched your library this way", where no shuffle happens when the search found nothing there. OthersTo is one search with two destinations: "search your library for up to two basic land cards, reveal them, put one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand". It is one search of up to UpTo cards (CR 701.23a — the whole search is one action), the first card found goes to To with Where and Tapped, and every other card found goes to OthersTo, tapped when OthersTapped is set. Never write it as two Searches: two searches see the library twice, so a player could find two cards that one search could not, and each would shuffle. Leave OthersTo null when every card found goes to the same zone, and leave OthersTapped false unless OthersTo is the battlefield, because nothing is tapped in another zone. Instead is one search whose destination depends on the card found: "search your library for a creature or land card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. If it's a land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped instead". It is still one search of one card (CR 701.23a); the card found is read against each entry's Matching filter in order, the first entry that admits it sends it to that entry's To, tapped as that entry says, and a card no entry admits goes to To with Tapped. Never two Searches and never an If around the Search: the condition is the card found, which nothing outside the search can name. An entry equal to the plain destination says nothing and is refused (L023).

Sequence.description: Instructions in order. "Draw two cards, then discard a card."

Store.description: A choice a player is asked to make, or a value an effect records for later steps.

Unless.description: "Counter target spell unless its controller pays {3}."

Unprepare.description: Unprepare, CR 702.180: the object loses the Prepared designation. Nothing happens if it was not prepared.

Unsupported.description: The translator could not express something in this vocabulary. A file containing this fails the linter and never reaches a game; the pipeline ranks these to find the next primitive.

Vote.description: Voting: each player votes for one option; the effect of the winning option runs, or per-vote effects.

AttackersAgainst.description: "two or more of those creatures are attacking you and/or planeswalkers you control": the creatures of the current declaration of attackers, CR 508.1, that are attacking the player Who names — and, while IncludingPermanentsTheyControl stands, the planeswalkers and battles that player controls, because a creature attacking one of those is attacking that player's side of the board and the printed phrase says "and/or". It counts the declaration, so it is read in the same moment as AttacksWithCreatures — the condition of an ability that trigger put on the stack, CR 603.4 — and it is not CountOf with an Attacking filter, which counts every attacking creature in the combat whoever declared it and whoever it is aimed at, so a two-player attack in a three-player game reads the wrong number. Clear the flag only for a card that names the player alone.

CardsDrawnThisTurn.description: "the number of cards you have drawn this turn", CR 121.1: a draw is one event per card, so this counts events and not the cards still in hand — a card drawn and then discarded, played or exiled is still a card that player drew this turn. It is per player and per turn. It is not CardsInHandOf, which counts a hand however those cards got there, and it is not the DrawnThisTurn predicate, which describes one card in a hand rather than counting a turn of draws; a card drawn and then discarded is counted here and matched by neither.

CardsInZoneOf.description: "the number of creature cards in your graveyard": cards in a zone, optionally filtered.

ChosenNumber.description: A number chosen earlier in the same effect with Choose.

CountOf.description: "the number of creatures you control": objects matching a filter.

CountersOn.description: Counters of one kind on an object; any kind when Counter is null.

CountersOnPlayer.description: Poison, energy, experience and other counters a player has.

Devotion.description: Devotion to one or more colors, CR 700.5: the number of mana symbols of those colors among the mana costs of permanents that player controls. Normally the colors are printed and go in Colors ("your devotion to black"). When the card instead reads "your devotion to the chosen color", leave Colors at Colorless and set ChosenColorKey to the key an earlier ChooseValue(ChooseWhat.Color, key) step stored the colour under; the colour is then read from that choice when the amount is counted. Never emit a fixed colour for a chosen one — the two are different cards.

Domain.description: The number of basic land types among lands a player controls.

GreatestAmong.description: "the greatest power among creatures you control". Of is read once per object Among admits, with that object bound as Self while it is read: "the greatest power among creatures you control" is Of: PowerOf(Self). It is not Triggering, which stays the trigger's own object throughout, and it is not the card the ability is printed on, which is out of reach inside the amount. The same binding rules TotalAmong.

HighestChosen.description: The highest number chosen in a secret simultaneous choice, CR 700.2 with 101.4: the greatest of the numbers the players chose under Key, read once they are revealed. Key names the ChooseNumberSecretly step of the same ability that asked for them, which is the only thing that produces it (L035). It is not ChosenNumber, which is one player choice and cannot say whose is greatest, and it is not GreatestAmong, which reads a characteristic off objects on the board. The players who chose it are PlayerWhoChose, and a tie names them all.

LandsEnteredThisTurn.description: The lands that entered the battlefield under a player control this turn, CR 121.1: the other event a turn keeps per player. Every land that entered counts, whether it was played from a hand (CR 305.1), put onto the battlefield by a search or returned by an effect, and a land that has since left still counts — the count is of the entering and not of the board. It is not CountOf over a land filter with an EnteredThisTurn predicate, which counts the lands still on the battlefield and reads a smaller number the moment one is sacrificed, and it is not the land drop the turn structure limits (CR 305.2), which counts plays and not entries.

LowestChosen.description: The lowest number chosen in that same secret choice, CR 700.2: the mirror of HighestChosen.

ManaSpentOnThis.description: Mana spent to cast this spell, CR 601.2h.

Stored.description: A number an earlier step produced: "the number of cards discarded this way".

TimesKicked.description: How many times this spell was kicked, CR 702.32b: multikicker's cost may be paid any number of times as the spell is cast, and "for each time it was kicked" counts those payments. Use this for multikicker and for replicate-shaped repeated optional costs; a card with plain kicker (CR 702.32a, paid once or not at all) asks WasKickedCondition instead, which is a yes or no. The KeywordAbility this counts must carry Repeatable, or nothing ever pays it twice.

TotalAmong.description: "the total power of creatures you control". Of is read once per object Among admits, with that object bound as Self while it is read, and the readings are summed: Of: PowerOf(Self). Self here is the candidate, never the source of the ability, and never Triggering — the same binding as GreatestAmong.

TriggeringDamage.description: "that much damage", "draw that many cards": how much damage the event that triggered this ability dealt, CR 603.10 — the trigger's own information, read as the ability resolves and not recomputed from the board. It is the amount half of every damage trigger, whether the ability is printed or was created as a DelayedTrigger this turn. It is not DamageDealtThisTurn, which totals a turn's damage and would count an earlier hit as well, and it is not a Stored key: no step of this card dealt the damage, so nothing on the card could have stored it. The ability it appears in must trigger on damage — DealsDamage, IsDealtDamage or PlayerIsDealtDamage, its own or its delayed trigger's — or there is no event to read and the amount is a lost sentence (L028).

X.description: The X paid or chosen for the spell or ability, CR 107.3.

Predicate.description: The long tail of object descriptions the fixed fields of ObjectFilter cannot express.

WouldBePutIntoZone.description: "If a card would be put into your graveyard from anywhere".

WouldBeginStep.description: "Skip your draw step", "if a player would begin their turn".

WouldDie.description: "If this creature would die, exile it instead."

WouldEnterBattlefield.description: "As this creature enters", "if a creature would enter under your control".

AddTypes.description: Adds card types, subtypes or supertypes in layer 4 (CR 613.1d) while keeping the ones already there: "is a creature in addition to its other types", "is also a Goblin". Set AllCreatureTypes when the object is every creature type at once — changeling (CR 702.72a) and any text reading "is every creature type" (CR 205.3d). Say it with that flag, never by listing creature types: the list changes with every set, and the engine derives it rather than carrying card data.

BecomesCopyOf.description: Layer 1: becomes a copy of another object, with the printed exceptions. ExceptThisAbility is the self-referential exception, CR 707.9b: "target land becomes a copy of this land, except it has this ability". "This ability" is the very ability the effect is part of, so the copy keeps a copy of it and can be used again — the exception is a flag and never a nested ability inside Except. Writing the ability out would nest one reading of it inside another with no end to the nesting, and a reader that stopped early would produce a copy that cannot copy, which is a different card. The ability the flag points at is the activated or triggered ability that created this effect (CR 707.9b names an ability of the object, and CR 109.5 says "this" means the object the ability is on). A static ability or a spell ability has no such ability to hand back — a spell ability goes to the graveyard with the card — so the flag on either is a lost sentence (L029).

CantBeBlocked.description: "can't be blocked", "can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less", "can't be blocked except by two or more creatures".

CantBeTargeted.description: Shroud and hexproof are keywords; this is the general form: "can't be the target of red spells".

CostModifier.description: "Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less": positive delta is an increase. OnlyColor is a reduction the printed line ties to one colour — "costs {W} less to cast" rather than "{1} less" (CR 601.2f, where the reduction is applied to the cost as it stands). The delta is then that many mana of that colour, and a cost with no such symbol left is not reduced further: a colourless spell is untouched by a {W} reduction, while a generic reduction of the same size would still have paid for it. Set GenericOnly false beside it, because the two flags describe the same half of the cost and a reduction cannot be generic-only and coloured at once (L030).

DamageDoesNotReduceLifeBelow.description: "Damage that would reduce your life total to less than 1 reduces it to 1 instead": a floor under a player's life total against damage, CR 120.4 (damage dealt to a player causes that player to lose that much life) with CR 119.3 (the life loss itself). It applies to the players a StaticAbility's Players or an ApplyToPlayer names, and it replaces only the damage event: the amount of damage is reduced so that the life total lands on Floor and no lower, and damage that leaves the total at or above the floor is dealt unchanged. It is not PreventDamage, which prevents a fixed amount or all of it whatever the life total is (CR 615), and it is not CantLoseGame, which lets the total fall and only stops the loss: a card that prints both sentences prints two abilities, and each is written as its own record. It is also not a life loss floor — Floor bites on damage alone, so a cost that pays life or an effect that says "lose life" is untouched, exactly as the printed line says.

ManaProducesAdditional.description: "Whenever you tap a Forest for mana, add an additional {G}."

MayBeginGameOnBattlefield.description: "If this card is in your opening hand, you may begin the game with it on the battlefield": the one kind of ability that functions before the game begins, CR 103.6. The StaticAbility that carries it names Where: Zone.Hand, because the hand is the zone the ability works from and a battlefield-scoped ability would never be read (L027). OnlyIf is the printed rider some of these carry — "and you're not the starting player" — read as the game is set up and never again. WithCounters is "with a luck counter on it", the counters the permanent begins the game with, and IfYouDo is the cost the offer carries: "if you do, exile a card from your hand". Leave each out when the card does not print it. The permission is one record and never a trigger: nothing has happened yet for a trigger to watch, there is no turn and no stack (CR 103.6), so an EntersBattlefield or AtStep reading of this line puts the card on the battlefield at a moment the rules do not offer.

MayPlayFromZone.description: "You may play lands from your graveyard", "you may cast spells from the top of your library". With WithoutPayingManaCost, "you may cast it this turn without paying its mana cost" (CR 118.9): the permission also waives the mana cost of the cast it allows. With PayLifeEqualToManaValueInstead, "if you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost": an alternative cost (CR 118.9) that the permission itself carries, paid at CR 601.2f in place of the mana cost, and only by a cast this permission allowed — a spell the player casts from hand pays as printed. The two sentences are one record, and this flag is their one spelling: never a second StaticAbility for the second sentence, and never SpellsCostLifeInsteadOfMana, which is every spell of a colour from any zone. A land played this way pays nothing either way. The two flags are two different alternative costs and a card prints one, so both set is a contradiction the linter refuses (L021).

MustBeBlocked.description: "All creatures able to block it do so."

OptionalAdditionalCost.description: "Spells your opponents cast have 'as an additional cost to cast this spell, you may pay {1}', and a spell paid for that way costs {2} less" — an optional additional cost this permanent imposes on other spells (CR 118.8: an additional cost is paid on top of the mana cost, and an optional one is a choice the caster makes as the spell is cast, CR 601.2b), with what paying it buys in IfPaid. Spells is the filter of spells the rider is added to and Who the caster it is offered to; Cost is the printed additional cost, announced and paid as part of casting (CR 601.2f) and not while the spell resolves. IfPaid is the continuous effect that applies to that spell only when the cost was paid — normally a CostModifier, which is the reduction the printed line gates on the payment. It is required (L030): an optional additional cost with nothing hanging on it is a cost no caster would ever choose to pay, so a reading that drops the reward has dropped the card. This is not Face.AdditionalCosts, which is the cost printed on the card paying it, and it is not AlternativeCost, which replaces the mana cost instead of adding to it. It is not MayPay either: this choice is made as the other spell is cast, and MayPay's is made as this card's own ability resolves.

PlayerCant.description: A prohibition that applies to a player rather than to an object: "your life total can't change", "you can't lose the game", "you can't be the target of spells", "prevent all damage that would be dealt to you". Apply it with a StaticAbility whose Players is set, or with ApplyToPlayer for a duration; the Selector-shaped To is not used for these. Several restrictions can be set at once because PlayerRestriction is a flag set. CantLoseGame, CantWinGame and CantGainLife stay as they are — they were already spelled that way in card files and mean exactly what they say; use this record for the restrictions they do not cover.

PlayerProtectionFromEverything.description: "You have protection from everything", CR 702.16j: the player can't be targeted by spells or abilities their opponents control, all damage that would be dealt to them is prevented, and they can't be enchanted. Protection on an object is the KeywordAbility Protection with its Of filter; this is the player-scoped form, which the keyword cannot carry because a player is not an object. Apply it through a StaticAbility with Players set, or ApplyToPlayer for a duration.

PreventDamage.description: Prevention, CR 615: all when Amount is null.

UnsupportedContinuous.description: An honest marker for a static ability's continuous effect this vocabulary cannot yet say, the ContinuousEffect half of Unsupported. A static ability's slot takes a ContinuousEffect and nothing else (CR 604.1), so without this record a clause the vocabulary cannot express has to be dropped, and a dropped clause is a card that plays wrongly with no sign of it. Reason says what could not be said and Text keeps the printed line for the judge. It lints as L001 exactly like Unsupported, so a file carrying one is never clean and never reaches a game: the marker is a request for a record, not a way to ship a half-read card. Never use it for a clause another record already says — check the vocabulary first, because a marker that could have been a spelling is worse than nothing.

AnyTarget.description: "Any target", CR 115.4: exactly one target chosen from among every creature, player, planeswalker and battle. This is the whole phrase in one selector, and it is the only spelling of it. Do not write it as a Target whose filter names Creature, Planeswalker and Battle beside a toPlayer, and do not write it as an open filter beside a toPlayer: the first cannot say the player half and the second lets the damage hit a land. On DealDamage it goes in To, and ToPlayer is then left out — To of AnyTarget already means "whichever of the four was chosen". The chosen target is announced as the spell or ability is put on the stack (CR 601.2c): an object target rides in the command's Targets and a player target in its TargetPlayers, so the two halves are one choice at cast time and the resolving effect deals its damage to whichever half the stack entry holds. Count, UpTo and Key are here for the same reason Target carries them: "any number of target creatures" has its counterpart in "up to one target", divided damage names several targets (CR 601.2d), and a later step refers back by Key. Count absent means one.

Attached.description: The object this Aura, Equipment or Fortification is attached to: "enchanted creature", "equipped creature".

Attachments.description: Objects attached to this one, optionally filtered.

Choose.description: A non-targeted choice: "choose a creature you control". The chooser picks when the effect resolves. Among is "from among them": the candidates are the objects that selector names — a Remembered key from an earlier reveal, look or exile — wherever they are, and Filter only narrows them ("permanent cards with mana value X or less from among them"). With Among set the filter's In is not read, because the candidates' zone is their own; writing one beside it is L022. This is the one spelling of a choice among remembered objects: never an IsRemembered predicate in the filter, whose zone would default to the battlefield and match none of the revealed cards. "Any number" is UpTo with no Count.

Each.description: "each creature", "all artifacts": every object matching the filter, no targeting.

RandomFrom.description: "a card at random from your hand".

Remembered.description: Objects an earlier step produced and remembered under a key: "the exiled card", "those tokens".

Self.description: This object: the permanent with the ability, or the spell being cast.

SourceOfDamage.description: The source of the damage a trigger or replacement is about.

Target.description: "target creature", "up to two target players' creatures". Key lets later steps refer back.

ThisSpellsTargets.description: The targets this spell or ability chose, for effects that refer back to them collectively.

Top.description: "the top card of your library", "the top three cards of target player's library".

Triggering.description: The object the trigger was about, or the other object involved: "that creature", "it", "the blocked creature".

AttachedPlayer.description: "Enchanted player": the player this Aura is attached to, CR 303.4f. Nobody when the source is attached to an object or to nothing.

ChoosePlayer.description: A non-targeted player choice: "choose a player".

DefendingPlayer.description: The player being attacked, or the controller of the planeswalker or battle being attacked.

PlayerWhoChose.description: "each player who chose the highest number", CR 700.2 with 101.4: every player whose secret choice under Key was the greatest of those revealed, or the least when Lowest stands. It names every one of them, because two players may choose the same number and the printed line reads "each player who chose". Key is the ChooseNumberSecretly step of the same ability that asked for the numbers, and nothing else produces it (L035). It is not PlayerWithMostOf, which reads an amount off the game for every player and knows nothing of a choice, and it is not ChosenPlayer, which is a player somebody picked.

PlayerWithMostOf.description: "the player with the most life", "the player who controls the most creatures".

TargetPlayer.description: "target player" or "target opponent". Names a key so later steps can refer back.

TriggeringPlayer.description: The player the trigger was about: the one who drew, discarded, was dealt damage.

You.description: The controller of the spell or ability.

AnyOfTriggers.description: "Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery": several events, one ability.

AtStep.description: "At the beginning of your upkeep", "at the beginning of each end step".

Attacks.description: "Whenever this creature attacks", "whenever a creature you control attacks a planeswalker".

AttacksWithCreatures.description: "Whenever an opponent attacks with creatures": one firing per declaration of attackers, CR 508.1, not one per attacking creature. It triggers once for the player By names when that player declares one or more attackers, whatever they attack and however many there are. It is not Attacks, which is CR 508.2 and fires once for each creature: a card that says "whenever an opponent attacks with creatures ... draw a card" draws one card for a three-creature attack, and written as Attacks it would draw three. It is not AttacksAlone either, which is the one-creature case. The "if two or more of those creatures are attacking you and/or planeswalkers you control" half is the ability's own If — a Compare over the AttackersAgainst amount, which counts this declaration's attackers aimed at one player and the permanents that player controls. The two are read at the same moment and neither is written as the other.

BecomesTarget.description: "Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability".

ChapterReached.description: A Saga chapter, CR 714. Chapter abilities are triggered abilities with this trigger.

CounterPlaced.description: "Whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are put on a creature you control"; Nth for "the third".

DealsDamage.description: "Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player", "whenever a source you control deals damage".

Dies.description: "Whenever a creature dies": put into a graveyard from the battlefield, CR 700.4.

Draws.description: "Whenever a player draws a card" (CR 121.1 — a draw is one event per card, so a player drawing two cards fires this twice). FirstEachTurn is "the first card they draw each turn"; DuringDrawStep pins the trigger to that step or excludes it. ExceptFirstInDrawStep is the printed exception "except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps": every draw fires the ability but that one, and the exception is about the player's own draw step, so a draw taken in someone else's draw step is not spared. It is the turn-based draw the exception is written to skip (CR 504.1), so a player who skips their draw step, or whose first draw of it is a second card, spares only the one draw that came first. It is the opposite of FirstEachTurn and the two never both hold (L033): one admits that draw alone, the other admits every draw but it. It is also not DuringDrawStep false, which refuses the whole step rather than its first draw.

EntersBattlefield.description: "When this creature enters", "Whenever another creature you control enters".

LandPlayed.description: Landfall: "whenever a land enters under your control" is EntersBattlefield; this is the play itself.

ManaSpent.description: "When that mana is spent to cast a spell, ...", CR 106.6: a mana instruction may create a delayed triggered ability that triggers when the mana it produced is spent (CR 603.7a). ManaKey is the Key of the AddMana in the same ability that produced that mana, which is how "that mana" is said without pointing at an object — mana is not an object. One delayed ability is created for each mana that AddMana produced (CR 106.6a). OnSpell narrows what the mana was spent on when the card does ("spent to cast a creature spell"); leave it null for "spent to cast a spell". Use it as the When of a DelayedTrigger the same resolution creates, never as a printed TriggeredAbility's own trigger: the mana it watches does not exist until the AddMana has run, and a standing trigger would have no key to match.

RoomUnlocked.description: A Room's door is unlocked, CR 709.5: the half gains its unlocked designation.

Searches.description: "Whenever an opponent searches their library", CR 701.23: the search itself is the event, and it fires once per search however many cards that search finds and whether it finds any. The search a card, spell or ability instructed is the one this watches (CR 701.23a); a player looking at their own library with no instruction to search is not searching. Who describes the searcher, so "an opponent" is a PlayerFilter with Opponent true — a filter and not a PlayerRef, because the trigger matches whoever searched rather than naming a player in advance, the same reading DealsDamage takes of ToPlayer. The library searched is the searcher's own, which is every printed sentence of this shape; a card that watches a search of someone else's library is a different trigger and does not exist yet. It is not the Search effect, which is this card telling a player to search, and it is not a ZoneChange or a Mills: nothing has left the library when this fires, and CR 701.23c shuffles only if the search moved a card.

TappedForMana.description: "Whenever a land you control is tapped for mana", CR 106.12a: the trigger fires when a mana ability of the permanent whose activation cost includes {T} resolves and produces mana (CR 106.12). What describes the permanent tapped. Set OfColor for "tapped for mana of a specified type" — "tapped for green mana" — and set OfChosenColorKey instead when the card reads "tapped for mana of the chosen color", naming the key an earlier ChooseValue(ChooseWhat.Color, key) stored the colour under. Set neither for "tapped for mana" of any type. Never set both: a card prints one colour restriction, and the fixed colour and the chosen one are different cards. This is the trigger half only. What the ability then does — "add an additional one mana of that color" — is an AddMana whose ManaProduction carries the same ChosenColorKey, so the two halves name the same choice. Every firing of this trigger stores the colour the permanent was actually tapped for under the key "tapped-for-mana-color", whatever OfColor or OfChosenColorKey say. That is how "add one mana of any type that land produced" is written: the ability's AddMana carries a ManaProduction whose ChosenColorKey is the literal string "tapped-for-mana-color", and there is no other spelling of it — the key names a colour the game observed, so no step on the card produces it and none has to.

ZoneChange.description: Any other zone change: "whenever a card is put into your graveyard from anywhere", CR 603.6. Every field but What is optional and each one set must hold. From names the zone the object left ("from your graveyard"), and NotFrom is the printed exception: "put into a graveyard from anywhere other than the battlefield" is To Graveyard with NotFrom Battlefield, and it is ONE trigger, never a ZoneChange wrapped in a condition about where the object was — the object is gone by the time the ability's condition is read (CR 603.10), so a condition there tests nothing. Set one or the other, never both: a card names the zone it cares about or the one it excludes. To is optional so that a trigger about leaving one zone for anywhere is one trigger too: "whenever a card leaves your graveyard" is From Graveyard with no To. Leave To out only then — a trigger with no From, no NotFrom and no To fires on every zone change in the game and is a lost sentence (L025). "Leaves the battlefield" keeps its own record, LeavesBattlefield, and "dies" keeps Dies.

ManaProduction.description: What a mana instruction produces. Fixed is printed mana ("{G}{G}"); otherwise one of the described choices. LandCouldProduce is "of any type that a land could produce" (CR 106.1b: a land's mana ability names the types it could produce). It surveys the lands you control unless LandCouldProduceOf describes a different set — "a land an opponent controls could produce" is LandCouldProduce: true with a filter of lands an opponent controls, and the survey is over exactly the lands that filter admits. Leave the filter null for the ordinary "a land you control could produce"; a filter that admits no land produces no mana, which is what an empty board means and not an error. ChosenColorKey is "mana of the chosen colour": the key of the earlier step that made the choice, and the colour travels with the key (CR 700.5, a choice a card made is remembered by the object). One firing of a TappedForMana trigger stores the colour the land was actually tapped for under the key "tapped-for-mana-color", so "add one mana of any type that land produced" is a ManaProduction whose ChosenColorKey is exactly that string and nothing else — no second AddMana, no Choose step, and no ColorOfAttachedOrTarget, which is about an attached object's colour rather than a colour a trigger observed. It is the one key the engine writes for a card rather than the card naming its own. ColorsOfRemembered is "one mana of any of that card's colours": the key of an earlier step that remembered the object whose colours are surveyed (CR 105.2, an object's colours are its own), typically a card exiled by this permanent. The player chooses among those colours when the mana is added; a remembered object with no colour produces no mana. Use it instead of AnyColor, which is every colour and would let a colourless card pay for anything.

Duration.description: How long an effect lasts, CR 611. A static ability's effect lasts while its source is on the battlefield and needs no duration; everything created by a resolving effect names one.

Mode.description: One printed mode: the line as printed in Text and what it does in Do. Cost is the price a mode carries when its list is spent against a Budget rather than counted — the mana the printed line puts in front of the mode, whose symbols are what the budget counts (CR 700.2). Nothing is paid for it: choosing the mode adds nothing to the spell's cost, and the price is read against the budget and nowhere else. A cost a player really pays to choose a mode is an additional cost on the face, not this. Leave it null for an ordinary numbered list of modes.

EmblemSpec.description: The emblem an effect creates, CR 114.1: a name for the log and the abilities it has.

TokenSpec.description: A token to create, CR 111. The pipeline fills it from Scryfall's all_parts and the token's own card object; ScryfallOracleId keeps the link.

SearchDestination.description: One "instead" destination of a Search, CR 701.23a: a card found that Matching admits goes to To rather than the search's own destination, tapped when Tapped is set, which only the battlefield allows. The filter carries no zone: it is read against the one card found, wherever the search looked. It is a plain object of these three parameters and has no "kind".

AttachedTo.description: The candidate is attached to what To names, CR 301.5c. The direction is candidate-first and never the other way round: the object being described is the attachment, and To is what it hangs on. AttachedTo(new Self()) therefore means "an Aura or Equipment attached to this permanent", which is what "Auras attached to it" says. It is not how "equipped creature" is written. That phrase names the creature this Equipment is attached to — the other end of the same link — and its spelling is the selector Attached, with no predicate at all. A filter of ObjectFilter(Also: AttachedTo(Self)) matches the Equipment's own Auras and matches the equipped creature never, so a card written that way silently affects nothing.

CanBlock.description: Able to block the given attacker right now.

CouldBlock.description: Could block the given creature if it were attacking, ignoring whether combat is happening.

DrawnThisTurn.description: A card its owner drew this turn, CR 121.1: "choose two cards in your hand that you drew this turn". A draw is a game event and the game remembers which cards were drawn, so this describes a card in a hand by how it got there and by nothing else. It is not EnteredThisTurn, which is a permanent entering the battlefield (CR 603.6a) and says nothing about a hand; and it is not a Remembered key, because the cards were drawn by another turn's step or by another ability, so no step of this card produced them. The filter it rides on carries the hand itself — In: Zone.Hand with a ControlledBy/OwnedBy of the player whose hand is meant — and this predicate only narrows that hand to the cards drawn this turn.

HasAbilityOfKind.description: Has an ability of the given kind: "a creature with a mana ability", "with an activated ability".

IsAttached.description: Attached to anything at all, or unattached when false.

IsOneOf.description: The candidate is one of the objects Of names: a selector said inside a filter. "Whenever equipped creature dies" is Dies with a filter of Also: IsOneOf(Attached) (CR 301.5c names the equipped creature from the Equipment's side), and "whenever that creature attacks" inside a delayed trigger is IsOneOf(Triggering). It is the general form of IsRemembered, which is IsOneOf(Remembered(key)) and stays the spelling for a remembered key; use this for the selectors that have no predicate of their own — Attached, Triggering, Commander, Top. It is not AttachedTo(Self), which runs the other way: that predicate admits the Auras and Equipment hanging on this permanent, never the creature this permanent hangs on, so a trigger written with it fires for the wrong objects.

IsPrepared.description: Carries the Prepared designation, CR 702.180: "prepared creatures you control", "if it's prepared". The designation is put on by the Prepare effect and taken off by Unprepare; it is not a counter, so WithCounter does not see it.

IsRemembered.description: The candidate is one of the objects an earlier step remembered under Key, CR 603.10: "that creature", "the exiled card", said inside a filter rather than as a selector. The Remembered selector names those objects to act on them; this predicate describes them, so a filter can require an object to be the remembered one and hold its other conditions at the same time — "prevent all damage that would be dealt by the chosen creature" is a filter of Also: IsRemembered(key), which no selector position can say. It reads a key another step produced and produces none itself, so the key must be remembered on the same face or the file does not lint (L003). Do not use it where a bare Remembered selector already fits: one spelling per idea, and a filter that names exactly one object and nothing else is that selector.

IsThisObject.description: The object this ability is printed on, and nothing else. "This" in a card's text always means the object the ability is on (CR 109.5), so a trigger that is about its own source says it with this predicate: "whenever this creature attacks" is Attacks with ObjectFilter(Also: IsThisObject), and "whenever this creature dies" is Dies with the same filter (CR 603.2 — a trigger's event is matched against its own source like any other object). Do not confuse it with Other, which means "another" and excludes this object, or with an unmarked filter, which matches every object it describes including this one. The selector Self is the same idea on the effect side: use Self to act on this object, IsThisObject to describe it inside a filter.

ProducesMana.description: A source that could produce mana of the given colors.

SharesTypeWith.description: Shares a card type — or, with CreatureTypeOnly, a creature type — with the object With names. This is how a relation between two objects the same effect touched is written, and it is the answer to the shape translators reach for a new record for: "search your library for two basic land cards that share a land type" is a Sequence whose first step searches and remembers the first card, and whose second step searches for one that shares a type with it — Sequence([Search(basicLand, Battlefield, RememberAs: "first"), Search(new ObjectFilter(Types: CardType.Land, Supertypes: Supertype.Basic, Also: new SharesTypeWith(new Remembered("first"), CreatureTypeOnly: false)), Zone.Battlefield)]). Remember plus this predicate expresses every "that share a ..." and "with the same ..." relation; SharesColorWith and SharesNameWith are the same pattern for colour and name.

TargetedBy.description: Currently targeted by the given object, typically Self.

Targets.description: "target spell that targets a permanent you control", CR 115.1: the candidate is a spell or ability on the stack that has chosen a target Of admits. It reads the targets the candidate announced (CR 601.2c), so a spell with no targets matches nothing here, and a spell whose only target has since become illegal still targeted it. It runs the opposite way from TargetedBy, which admits the object a spell points at; this admits the spell doing the pointing, and a filter that means one and writes the other matches the wrong half of the same pair. The filter it rides on carries the spell itself — Spell true, with In Stack where the card names the zone — and a filter that says this of a permanent describes an object that cannot target (L037).

ForAsLongAs.description: "for as long as you control an artifact".

UntilLeaves.description: "for as long as that creature remains on the battlefield".

UntilStep.description: "until the beginning of your next upkeep", "until the end of your next turn".
